A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Rank-Learner: Orthogonal Ranking of Treatment Effects. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–F are readable, and corresponding methods, proofs, experiments, and displays can be matched despite additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments, including ranking performance, nuisance estimation, pair subsampling, overlap sensitivity, and a tree-ranker comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds CRITEO, ACIC/IHDP, additional baseline comparisons, and several robustness and sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The core two-stage objective, orthogonal pseudo labels, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix F.2.2 adds an evaluated variant that samples pairs proportionally to their correction weights instead of uniformly. Uniform sampling remains the main procedure, and label clipping was already present in v1.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original synthetic, MovieLens, MIMIC-III, and CPS coverage, while adding CRITEO advertising data with observed binary website-visit outcomes and treatment-effect ranking on ACIC and IHDP. These substantially broaden evaluation beyond the original simulated treatment/outcome constructions.

E2.justification: The main T-learner, DR-learner, and plug-in ranker comparisons remain. The expanded synthetic comparison in v2 Table 12 retains the tree ranker and adds DR ranker, PairNet, and FlexTENet. DR ranker constructs pairwise targets from doubly robust pseudo outcomes and is distinct from the retained pointwise DR-learner.

E3.justification: The original main experimental settings are largely retained. v2 adds CRITEO confounded-training/randomized-testing procedures, AUUC evaluation, 10,000 training and 5,000 validation samples, and three test sizes. Appendix F.4 adds a separate CATENets-style implementation for the synthetic comparison, ACIC heterogeneity-based selection, the first 50 IHDP replications, and within-replication normalized AUTOC and win rates. These are additional or replaced experimental settings, not evidence that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained pair-count, nuisance-quality, and overlap analyses, v2 adds weighted versus uniform pair sampling, deliberately misspecified linear nuisance models, a nuisance-perturbation diagnostic for the clipped loss, and smoothing-parameter sensitivity across training sizes. Tables 10–11 and Figures 7–8 address practical robustness questions not tested in v1.

E5.justification: Five-seed means with standard deviations in tables and standard errors in performance plots remain the usual reporting practice. Appendix E.3 newly specifies that CRITEO test sets are redrawn for each seed, incorporating test-sample variation unlike the fixed test sets used previously. No increase in the retained experiments' run counts or new significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: New benchmark, baseline, and robustness outcomes substantially expand the results. Existing values also change: Table 3 revises Rank-Learner AUTOC from 0.94±0.21 to 1.00±0.19 at n=100 and from 1.30±0.03 to 1.31±0.01 at n=500; Table 4 revises DR-learner MIMIC-III AUTOC from 1.16 to 1.17. The expanded tree comparison replaces results under a different Rank-Learner configuration and removes its policy-value rows. New findings include highest relative AUTOC on both ACIC and IHDP, although IHDP overall win rate favors DR-learner, 42% versus 40%.

T1.justification: The causal assumptions, Theorems 5.1–5.2, and derivations and proofs in Appendices B–D are substantively unchanged. Appendix F.3.3 introduces the mathematical definition of a finite-difference gradient-norm sensitivity diagnostic in Equation 137. This is a limited formal addition, not a new proof of orthogonality for the clipped objective.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central claims: direct, model-agnostic, Neyman-orthogonal treatment-effect ranking, robustness to nuisance estimation errors, and empirical outperformance. The expanded conclusion reiterates these contributions and summarizes additional supporting experiments rather than redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 newly explains that rankings alone cannot support decisions requiring treatment effects to exceed a numerical threshold. Appendix F.3.3 explicitly acknowledges that clipping modifies the ideal orthogonal objective. v2 also discusses low-heterogeneity benchmarks as less suitable for ranking and suggests that existing pair-dependent corrections explain the limited benefit of weighted sampling. These qualify and extend the retained interpretation.

D1.justification: The reported code location changes from an anonymous repository to an identified GitHub repository. v2 documents CRITEO's selective sampling, covariates, weighted binary losses, and evaluation details, and provides CATENets implementation pointers. Conversely, v1's explicit tree-ranker tuning grid and shared-nuisance-estimate statement are omitted. Common hardware, neural-network, optimizer, and hyperparameter-search details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds an uplift-modeling discussion in Appendix A.2, distinguishes budget-based ranking from threshold-based policies, and mentions orthogonal learning for preference-based LLM evaluation. References are added for these connections and the new benchmarks and baselines. The central positioning as the first model-agnostic orthogonal two-stage treatment-effect ranker remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting and reorganization concentrate on the experimental discussion and Appendices A, E, and F. Appendix F now groups material into main results, computational efficiency, robustness, and additional comparisons; the conclusion becomes an expanded numbered section. The abstract, main methodological narrative, and proof structure are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the CRITEO table and its appendix repeat, pair-sampling and misspecification tables, the ACIC/IHDP table, and two three-panel diagnostic figures. v1 Table 7 becomes the expanded, AUTOC-only Table 12 with additional comparator rows and second-best highlighting. Existing displays are also relocated, including Table 4 and the appendix subsampling and overlap figures.

improvement.justification: v1's validation centers on designed synthetic and semi-synthetic settings with limited comparators. v2 substantially strengthens empirical support through observed CRITEO outcomes, ACIC/IHDP, stronger neural baselines, and tests of misspecification, smoothing, and the implemented clipped loss. The new applicability qualifications also improve interpretation. These gains outweigh the loss of explicit tree-ranker tuning details, although ACIC selection and CATENets settings remain incompletely specified, and the clipping diagnostic does not establish exact orthogonality.
